## 🌟 Summary
Version 8.4.181 focuses on making dataset loading, annotation, tracking, and inference more reliable, with several performance and compatibility improvements. No model architecture changes are included.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **Fixed data-pipeline edge cases:** Dataset discovery now prioritizes `.yaml` files before `.yml` files, preventing unrelated YAML files from breaking dataset loading. `.txt` and `.csv` prediction-source lists work regardless of filename capitalization, and dataset hashing now supports filenames with non-UTF-8 characters.
- **Improved automatic annotation:** `auto_annotate` now names label files using the detector’s prediction output path, helping keep labels matched to images with the same filename stem.
- **Made rotated-box tracking steadier:** Tracked object angles now stay consistent between frames instead of unexpectedly flipping, making angle-based tracking output easier to use.
- **Reduced segmentation memory overhead:** Native mask processing writes results into a preallocated output stack, avoiding extra full-size copies. A related filtering change also avoids repeated GPU-to-CPU synchronization.
- **Fixed small-image depth output:** Depth maps for one-row, one-column, and 1×1 images now retain their expected two-dimensional shape.
- **Improved training metrics on shared GPU hosts:** Platform system metrics report the GPUs used by the training run, rather than including unrelated GPUs on the same machine.
- **Updated compatibility checks and guidance:** PyTorch–Torchvision checks cover newer releases, JetPack detection includes JetPack 7.2, and TensorRT 11 DLA limitations are clarified. CI also tests newer Python versions with recent PyTorch releases.
- **KPTTracker is not part of this release:** Its earlier addition was reverted.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- Dataset setup and prediction workflows should fail less often on common filename and file-format edge cases.
- Tracking, depth prediction, and segmentation results are more consistent, including for unusual image sizes and rotated objects.
- Segmentation may use less temporary memory, while Platform GPU charts more accurately reflect each run.
- Updated compatibility checks and documentation should make it easier to identify supported software and hardware combinations.

* Refresh stale version lookups: torchvision pairing, JetPack 7.2, TensorRT 11 DLA by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26728
* Simplify is_jetson JetPack lookup and run each SlowTests torch shard on its newest Python by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26733

## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.180 improves pose-aware training for YOLO26-pose and fixes several edge cases in data loading, result export, tracking, and visualization.**

## 📊 Key Changes
- 🧍 **YOLO26-pose assignment now considers keypoint quality as well as box overlap.** The training process uses both bounding-box overlap and keypoint OKS when selecting positive matches, resolving conflicts, and creating confidence targets. Ground truths with no visible keypoints continue to use box overlap alone. This behavior is enabled by default and applies only to YOLO26-pose; YOLOv8/YOLO11 pose loss behavior is unchanged.
- 📹 **More robust data-source and dataset handling.** Stream manifests are recognized regardless of extension capitalization, and extensionless URLs returning images are treated as single images. Dataset lookup now accepts `.yml` as well as `.yaml`; conversion also handles non-ASCII cache paths more reliably and skips unlabeled DOTA background images.
- 📄 **Safer result and validation exports.** `Results.summary()` now returns an empty list instead of failing when there are no boxes or oriented boxes. Validation text labels use split-relative image paths, preventing different images with the same filename from being merged into one label file.
- 🎥 **Improved tracking under camera rotation.** Camera-motion compensation now updates box sizes and oriented-box angles appropriately, reducing geometry errors that could accumulate in tracks.
- 🖼️ **Fixed multiline text rendering with Pillow 13.** Classification and other visualizations that draw multiline text are less likely to crash.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🎯 **Better alignment between pose training and pose evaluation:** YOLO26-pose can favor detections with more accurate keypoints, not just better-fitting boxes. This may improve pose quality and confidence ranking.
- 🛠️ **Fewer workflow interruptions:** Common edge cases in data loading, exports, and plotting are handled more safely.
- 📈 **More dependable outputs:** Tracking boxes retain more appropriate geometry during camera motion, and validation labels remain distinct for images from different folders.

* Handle case-insensitive stream manifests by @Vaishnavi220506 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26721

## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.179 focuses on export reliability and inference correctness**, led by a compatibility fix for RKNN on Rockchip devices. It also improves SAM, validation, benchmarking, and training stability.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **RKNN export compatibility:** Caps `rknn-toolkit2` at versions below 2.5, because version 2.5.0 can fail to build YOLOv8 and YOLO11 models across Rockchip targets, and YOLO26 on RK3588. The RKNN smoke test now uses `imgsz=64` to better catch this failure.
- **SAM improvements:** Segment-everything prompts now target the image area rather than letterbox padding, avoiding empty masks and improving results on narrow images. Mask resizing is also handled centrally in the prompt encoder.
- **More reliable export and training:** JetPack 6 with TensorRT 10.3 now returns an actionable error for unsupported INT8 exports with embedded NMS. YOLO26 pose loss is more numerically stable, and `torch.compile` falls back gracefully on CUDA systems without working Triton.
- **More accurate evaluation:** RT-DETR validation now filters out unrequested classes before applying the detection limit. YOLOE and YOLO-World benchmarks use the dataset’s class vocabulary for a fairer comparison between PyTorch and exported models.
- **Performance and robustness fixes:** TorchScript warmup now happens before timed CPU inference, ZIP archives with a root `./` entry no longer crash extraction, and transient GitLab mirror failures get one retry.
- **Safeguards and documentation:** An unsafe TorchScript graph rewrite was removed to preserve correct model outputs. Documentation also clarifies ONNX INT8 quantization and updates guidance for Roboflow imports and Platform features.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- **Rockchip users** avoid a known-broken RKNN dependency version, while the stronger smoke test is more likely to catch similar export issues before release.
- **SAM users** should see fewer padding-related empty masks and more reliable prompts across different image shapes.
- **Model developers** get clearer failure messages and more dependable validation, benchmarking, and training behavior.
- **No new model architecture is introduced** in this release; the main impact is improved compatibility, correctness, and usability.

## What's Changed
* Fix cohort regressions at their owners and remove test growth by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26698
* Handle ZIP root directory entries without IndexError by @Nikhila-Dhevi-R in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26712
* Raise actionable diagnostic for TensorRT 10.3 INT8 nms=True exports on JetPack 6 by @JohnnyWilson16 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26711
